payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Detra, Gavin, Gudrun, Malika

payload.content: Hi team! Gavin here. Looking at the devops tasks, I'm strongly considering ISSUE-0002::review (3.5h effort, devops focus). It's my best fit with lowest cost (3.39). Any conflicts or other devops tasks others are eyeing?

Hi team! Gudrun here. I have UI-UX design skills (0.73) and 8h availability. Looking at ISSUE-0001 tasks which include ui-ux-design tags. The triage task (2.4h) seems most feasible with my cost at 5.16. I'm considering ISSUE-0001::triage - any conflicts? Gavin, I see you're looking at ISSUE-0002::review. Should work well since we're on different issues.

Hi team! Malika here. I have UI-UX design skills (0.72) and 4h availability. Looking at the tasks, I'm considering ISSUE-0001::triage (2.4h effort) since it matches my skills and has the lowest cost for me at 5.21. The other ISSUE-0001 tasks would be too much effort given my availability - implement (6h), review (3h), docs (3h), and test (4.2h) would all exceed or max out my capacity. ISSUE-0002 tasks are pure devops which don't match my skill set well at all. Gudrun, I see you're also considering ISSUE-0001::triage - should we coordinate? I'm flexible if you prefer this task and I can look for alternatives.

Update: After reviewing the tasks more carefully, I notice that ISSUE-0001::review (3h effort) and ISSUE-0001::docs (3h effort) would also fit within my 4h availability, though they'd leave me with only 1h buffer. My costs would be 6.51 for either of these vs 5.21 for triage. Since Gudrun is also interested in triage, I'm open to taking review or docs instead if that helps the team coordination. These would still leverage my UI-UX design skills for the devops improvement work.

Hi team! Detra here. I have strong UI-UX design skills (0.99) and 9h availability. Looking at ISSUE-0001 tasks which are perfect for my skill set. I'm most interested in ISSUE-0001::implement (6h, cost 10.12) since it's the highest priority critical task and I have the skills to deliver quality work. However, I'm also open to ISSUE-0001::test (4.2h, cost 7.08) or ISSUE-0001::review/docs (3h each, cost 5.06) if others prefer implement. Gudrun and Malika - since you're both looking at triage, perhaps I can take a different subtask to avoid conflicts? Gavin - your ISSUE-0002::review choice looks good, no overlap with my preferences.

Thanks for the updates everyone! Here's how I see our coordination shaping up:

- Gavin: ISSUE-0002::review (confirmed, devops focus)
- Gudrun & Malika: Both interested in ISSUE-0001::triage - suggest Malika takes it (better cost), Gudrun considers ISSUE-0001::review or docs
- Detra: ISSUE-0001::implement would be great fit for your UI-UX skills

This would give us good coverage across both critical issues. Any objections to this arrangement? (phase=planning, iter=1)

Hi team! Following up on Gavin's suggested coordination: I'm happy to take ISSUE-0001::review (3h effort, cost 6.45) instead of triage, since Malika has a better cost for triage (5.21 vs my 5.16). This would give us: Gavin on ISSUE-0002::review, Malika on ISSUE-0001::triage, Detra on ISSUE-0001::implement, and me on ISSUE-0001::review. This covers both critical issues efficiently with good skill matches. Any other adjustments needed? (phase=planning, iter=1)

Hi team! Thanks for the coordination efforts. I agree with the proposed arrangement: Gavin on ISSUE-0002::review, Detra on ISSUE-0001::implement, Gudrun on ISSUE-0001::review, and me on ISSUE-0001::triage. This gives us good coverage on both critical issues while matching skills effectively. The only thing I'm wondering is whether we should also consider assigning someone to ISSUE-0001::docs (3h) or ISSUE-0001::test (4.2h) since we have critical priority tasks still available? Or is the preference to keep it to one task per agent to maximize completion across different issues? Happy to proceed with the current plan either way - just wanted to check if others think we should optimize differently for the remaining tasks. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Actually, let me clarify my position - I'm happy with the current arrangement where I take ISSUE-0001::triage (2.4h, cost 5.21). This fits perfectly within my 4h availability and has the best cost for me. The remaining ISSUE-0001 tasks (docs and test) can be picked up by others if they have capacity, or we can focus on completing the tasks we've already identified as good fits. Ready to proceed with this plan unless anyone has other suggestions! (phase=planning, iter=1)

Hi team! Based on our coordination discussions, I'm confirmed with taking ISSUE-0001::implement (6h, cost 10.12). This leverages my strong UI-UX design skills on the critical priority implementation task. Current plan looks solid: Gavin on ISSUE-0002::review, Malika on ISSUE-0001::triage, Gudrun on ISSUE-0001::review, and me on ISSUE-0001::implement. This gives us excellent coverage of both critical issues with good skill matches. Ready to execute! (phase=planning, iter=1)
Final update from me: I'm locked in on ISSUE-0002::review as discussed. Our coordination plan looks solid with good coverage on both critical issues. Ready to execute!

Final confirmation from Gudrun: I'm locked in on ISSUE-0001::review (3h effort, cost 6.45). This works well with our coordinated plan - Gavin on ISSUE-0002::review, Malika on ISSUE-0001::triage, Detra on ISSUE-0001::implement, and me on ISSUE-0001::review. Ready to execute phase! (phase=planning, iter=1)

Malika here with my final confirmation: I'm locked in on ISSUE-0001::triage (2.4h effort, cost 5.21). This fits perfectly within my 4h availability and leverages my UI-UX design skills on the critical priority task. Our coordinated plan is now complete: Gavin on ISSUE-0002::review, me on ISSUE-0001::triage, Detra on ISSUE-0001::implement, and Gudrun on ISSUE-0001::review. Ready to execute phase!

Final coordination check from Gavin: I'm confirmed on ISSUE-0002::review. It looks like we have excellent coverage planned - we'll complete 4 critical tasks across both issues with strong skill matches. For any remaining agents still deciding, the available tasks are ISSUE-0001::docs, ISSUE-0001::test, and ISSUE-0002::implement/test tasks. Great teamwork everyone! (phase=planning, iter=1)

Team - I notice a potential issue: Both Gavin and Olevia have confirmed ISSUE-0002::review. This would be a duplicate assignment which violates our rules. Gavin, Olevia - can you clarify who is taking this task? We need to resolve this before execution. Otherwise our coordination looks good for the other tasks.

Malika here - I see the conflict Gavin mentioned. Looking at the communications, it appears Olevia hasn't actually posted on our blackboard yet, so I'm not sure where that duplicate assignment is coming from. 

To clarify my position: I'm still confirmed on ISSUE-0001::triage as we coordinated. The plan we agreed on was:
- Gavin: ISSUE-0002::review
- Malika: ISSUE-0001::triage  
- Detra: ISSUE-0001::implement
- Gudrun: ISSUE-0001::review

This gives us good coverage without conflicts on our blackboard. If there are agents on other blackboards also considering ISSUE-0002::review, that might explain the potential duplicate.

I'm ready to execute with ISSUE-0001::triage - it's the best fit for my 4h availability and UI-UX skills at cost 5.21.

One more thought - if there are indeed cross-blackboard conflicts with ISSUE-0002::review, perhaps Gavin could consider ISSUE-0002::test (4.9h effort) instead? That would resolve any potential duplicate while still keeping him on the critical ISSUE-0002 tasks. Just a suggestion in case the conflict can't be resolved otherwise. 

I'm sticking with ISSUE-0001::triage as my final choice - it's the optimal assignment for me given my constraints and skills.
